meta.description: Thapsus-HR is the simpler, fairer HR platform for growing companies across the UK, EU and US.

hero.eyebrow: HR for the UK, EU and US
hero.title: People, time and compliance. Calmly handled.
hero.lead: One place for employee records, time off, rotas and the rules of every country you hire in, with your data kept in the region you choose.

regions.uk: Data stays in London, with backups across availability zones.
regions.eu: Data stays in Frankfurt; backup copies only within the EU.
regions.us: Data stays in Ohio; backup copies only within the US.

features.title: Everything HR needs, nothing it does not.
features.lead: Built for ten people or two hundred thousand, with the same calm interface.

people.title: People and organisation
people.body: Effective-dated records, multiple legal entities and an org chart that stays fast at any size.

timeOff.title: Time off and absence
timeOff.body: Policies per country, public holidays, sickness tracking and statutory rules kept current.

rota.title: Rotas and time
rota.body: Build rotas, swap shifts and clock in from any phone, with working-time rules built in.

compliance.title: Compliance centre
compliance.body: Right to work, I-9, pay transparency and more, with a feed of what changed and what to do.

residency.title: Your data stays in your region.
residency.body: Choose where your company lives when you sign up. Every record, file, backup and email for your people stays there.

pricing.title: Transparent pricing
pricing.body: Published prices by company size. Monthly plans you can leave at any time.

export.title: Your data, always
export.body: Export everything whenever you like, in open formats.

support.title: Real people
support.body: Responsive human support, with clear response times on every plan.

cta.title: Bring calm to HR in an afternoon.

mock.caption: The Thapsus-HR people directory showing three fictional employees.

security.passkeyBody: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN. Passkeys cannot be phished.

certificate.statement: The signer confirmed they had read the document above and agreed to sign it electronically. Thapsus-HR recorded the signer, time, IP address, device and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the exact document signed. Any change to the document changes its fingerprint.

documents.title: Documents
documents.signBody: Read the document first. Your name, the time, your IP address and a fingerprint of the exact document are recorded.
documents.consent: I have read this document and agree to sign it electronically.

admin.name: Name
admin.readOnly: You can view these settings. Ask a workspace owner if something needs to change.
admin.secretOnce: Copy it now and store it somewhere safe. For your security it will not be shown again.

sso.lead: Let people sign in with your identity provider. Test a connection before you require it.
sso.noneBody: Add an OIDC or SAML connection below.
sso.oidcHint: Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta and most modern providers.
sso.samlHint: For providers that only support SAML.
sso.nameHint: Shown to administrators only, for example the provider’s name.
sso.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again.
sso.scopesHint: Leave blank for openid email profile.
sso.entryPointHint: The single sign-on URL from your provider’s SAML set-up.
sso.idpCertHint: Paste the provider’s X.509 signing certificate (PEM or Base64).
sso.jitHint: Only for people whose email address is on a verified domain. Everyone else needs an invitation.
sso.addBody: You will get the values to enter in your identity provider straight away.
sso.createdOidc: Add this redirect URI to the application in your identity provider, then test sign-in.
sso.createdSaml: Enter these values in your identity provider’s SAML application, then test sign-in.
sso.deleteBody: People will no longer be able to sign in with this connection. This cannot be undone.
sso.enforceBody: When required, people can only sign in through your identity provider: passwords, passkeys and email links stop working.
sso.requiredBody: Everyone signs in with single sign-on.
sso.optionalBody: People can also sign in with a password, passkey or email link.
sso.requireBody: Make sure you have tested a connection with your own account first, or you could lock everyone out.
sso.enforcedOff: Single sign-on is no longer required.

policy.lead: Rules for every sign-in to this workspace. Administrators must always use two-step verification.
policy.sessionsBody: People are signed out after a period without activity, and always after the maximum session length.
policy.lockoutBody: After too many failed attempts the account is locked for a while, which slows down password guessing.
policy.mfaBody: Two-step verification is always required for administrator roles.
policy.trustIdpMfa: Trust two-step verification done by the identity provider
policy.trustIdpMfaHint: People who sign in with single sign-on are not asked again.

scim.lead: Connect your directory (for example Microsoft Entra ID or Okta) so accounts are created, updated and deactivated automatically.
scim.endpointBody: Enter this base URL as the tenant URL in your directory’s provisioning settings.
scim.tokensBody: Your directory authenticates with a secret token. Create one per directory and revoke it when it is no longer used.
scim.name: Token name
scim.nameHint: For example, the directory it is for.
scim.revokeBody: Your directory will stop provisioning straight away until you give it a new token.

support.lead: Thapsus support can only see your workspace while you allow it. Every access is recorded in your audit log.
support.grantBody: Ask the Thapsus support person for their staff ID. Access ends automatically.
support.staffIdHint: A code like 3f2b8c1e-…, given to you by Thapsus support.
support.levelReadHint: Support can look but cannot change anything.
support.levelWriteHint: Support can also make changes for you. Every change is recorded.
support.reasonHint: For example, the support ticket this is for.
support.listBody: Revoke access as soon as it is no longer needed.
support.none: Support has never been given access
support.revokeBody: Thapsus support will lose access to your workspace straight away.

approvals.lead: For each kind of request, the first chain whose condition matches decides who approves it, step by step.
approvals.noneBody: Without a chain, requests are approved automatically.
approvals.orderHint: Chains are checked in order of priority; the first that applies is used.
approvals.subject: Request type
approvals.enabledHint: Turn off to stop using it for new requests.
approvals.chainCondition: Only use this chain when a condition is met
approvals.stepCondition: Only include this step when a condition is met
approvals.conditionFieldHint: Pick from the list or type a field name.
approvals.appliesAlways: Used for every request of this type.
approvals.timeoutHint: Optional. If nobody decides in time, the request is escalated.
approvals.needsApprover: Choose the role or person for every approver.

workflows.lead: Checklists of tasks that start when someone joins, leaves or moves. Due dates count from that day.
workflows.noneBody: Create an onboarding checklist to get started.
workflows.entityHint: Use it only for people in this entity.

autoStartHint.onboarding: Starts when someone is added with a start date.
autoStartHint.offboarding: Starts when a leaver is recorded.

workflows.dueOffsetHint: Use a negative number for days before, 0 for the day itself.
workflows.reminderHint: Optional. Leave blank for the default reminder.
workflows.reminderOnDay: On the day it is due
workflows.needsAssignee: Choose the role or person for every task.

delegations.lead: While you are away, a colleague can approve requests that would come to you.
delegations.newBody: Your delegate gets your approval tasks for these days. You can still approve too.
delegations.endBeforeStart: The last day must be on or after the first day.
delegations.receivedBody: Approvals you can make on a colleague’s behalf.
delegations.noneGiven: You have not delegated your approvals
delegations.noneReceived: Nobody has delegated their approvals to you.
delegations.endBody: They will no longer receive your approvals.

leave.lead: Policies decide how much leave people get and how it builds up. The most specific policy applies: assigned, then legal entity, then country, then everyone.
leave.typesBody: Set up from your country’s rules when the workspace was created.
leave.policiesBody: Assign a policy to people to override the default for their entity or country.
leave.assignBody: From this date the policy replaces any other policy for the same leave type.

accrualText.annual_upfront: {amount} a year, given at the start of the year

method.annual_upfront: All at the start of the leave year

methodHint.annual_upfront: The full entitlement is available on the first day of the leave year.
methodHint.monthly: One twelfth of the entitlement is added each month.
methodHint.per_hour_worked: For irregular hours and part-year workers, from recorded hours or timesheets.

leave.waitingHint: Days after the start date before leave can be booked.
leave.carryOverOn: Allow unused leave to carry over
leave.carryExpiresHint: Optional. Leave blank if carried-over leave does not expire.
leave.negativeHint: 0 means people cannot book more than they have.
leave.proRata: Pro rata for part-time and part-year
leave.proRataHint: Entitlement follows FTE and the days employed in the year.
leave.includesPublicHolidays: Public holidays come out of this entitlement
leave.includesPublicHolidaysHint: For example, 28 days including bank holidays.

roundingText.up_half_day: Rounded up to the next half day
roundingText.nearest_half_day: Rounded to the nearest half day
roundingText.up_whole_day: Rounded up to the next whole day

leave.entityHint: Leave as all entities to use the country or everyone.
leave.countryHint: Two-letter code, for example GB. Leave blank for every country.
leave.toilHint: Time off in lieu is earned through balance adjustments on a person’s profile.
leave.addBody: Statutory minimums come from the official rules for the country; you will be warned if a policy is below them.
leave.belowMinimum: This policy is below the statutory minimum of {amount}. It was saved, but check it before assigning it.
leave.checkBody: See the balance a person has today under the policies that apply to them.

balances.caption: Leave balances for {name}
balances.adjustBody: Add or take away leave, for example time off in lieu earned or a correction. It is recorded with your reason.
balances.amountHint: In the policy’s unit. Use a negative number to take leave away.

calendars.lead: Closure days are treated like public holidays for the people they apply to.
calendars.addBody: For example, a winter closure for one legal entity or a site’s local holiday.

absence.lead: Absence settings for sickness and family leave, and alerts when absence reaches a level you choose.
absence.policyBody: Company rules on top of the statutory rules.
absence.fitNote: Ask for a fit note after (calendar days)
absence.fitNoteHint: Leave blank to use the statutory rule for each country.
absence.fmlaBody: How the 12-month FMLA leave year is measured for everyone in the United States.

fmlaMethods.forward_from_first_leave_date: 12 months from the first day of leave
fmlaMethods.rolling_backward_from_leave_date: Rolling 12 months back from each day of leave

absence.publicAgencyHint: Public agencies are covered by FMLA whatever their size.
absence.triggersBody: Alerts HR, and the person’s manager if you choose, when sickness absence reaches a threshold.
absence.bradfordHint: Spells × spells × days. Optional if you set spells.
absence.spellsHint: Separate absences. Optional if you set a Bradford score.
absence.needsThreshold: Set a Bradford score, a number of spells, or both.
absence.coverBody: Checks time off requests so enough people stay on duty.
absence.minPresentHint: People who must still be working on each day.
absence.enforcement: When a request would break the rule
absence.warnHint: The request can still be approved.
absence.blockHint: The request cannot be made for those days.

time.lead: Working-time rules come from the official rules for each country. Here you choose how strictly they are applied.
time.rulesBody: Rest periods, breaks and weekly limits are checked whenever a shift is created or changed.
time.enforcement: When a shift breaks a rule
time.warnHint: The shift is saved and the problem is shown.
time.blockHint: The shift is not saved until it follows the rules.
time.weekStartHint: Used for weekly hours, overtime and timesheets.
time.geofenceBody: Check that people are at their site when they clock in or out. It is off unless you turn it on for a country, and workers see your notice first.
time.geofenceOff: Geofencing is off in every country.
time.turnOffBody: Location will no longer be checked when people clock in or out there.
time.addCountry: Turn on geofencing for a country
time.noticeHint: Explain what is checked and why. Workers see it before their location is read.
time.noticeRequired: Write the notice workers will see in at least one language.
time.sitesBody: Geofencing compares a clock-in with the area of the person’s location.
time.siteBody: The centre of the site and how far from it a clock-in still counts as on site.
time.clockingBody: Limits for shared kiosks, offline clocking and timesheet checks.

leaver.title: Start a leaver for {name}
leaver.body: Their access, pay, contract and reporting lines end after the last working day. The offboarding checklist starts automatically.
leaver.done: Leaver started for {name}. Last working day: {date}.

transfer.title: Transfer {name}
transfer.body: Choose only what changes. The transfer checklist starts automatically.
transfer.blankKeeps: Leave blank to keep the current job title.
transfer.nothing: Choose at least one thing to change.

timeOff.icsCopied: Calendar link copied. Paste it into your calendar app to subscribe.
timeOff.noEmployee: Your account is not linked to an employee record.

sickness.fitNoteRequired: Sickness recorded. A fit note is needed for an absence this long.

rota.blocked: This shift would break a working-time rule, so it was not saved.

rota.noTemplates: No templates yet. Build a week, then save it as a template.
rota.openedInstead: {count} shifts were left open because they would break a working-time rule.

rota.noOpenShifts: No open shifts you can pick up this week.

rota.searchHint: Type at least two letters of their name.
rota.swapSent: Swap offered. Your colleague needs to accept it, then your manager approves it.
rota.claimLine: You asked for the open shift on {date}
rota.swapTo: You offered your shift on {date} to {name}
rota.swapAccepted: Accepted. Your manager will review it.

working_time.daily_rest: Less than the minimum daily rest between shifts
working_time.rest_break: Rest break shorter than the legal minimum
working_time.max_weekly_hours: Average weekly hours over the legal limit
working_time.time_recording: No recorded time on a scheduled day

availability.unavailable: Marked as unavailable on this day
availability.outside_window: Outside the hours they are available

clock.title: Clock in
clock.noEmployee: Your account is not linked to an employee record.
clock.offline: You are offline. Punches are saved on this device and sent when you are back online.
clock.rejected: {count} punches could not be saved. Ask your manager to correct your time.
clock.geofenceWhen: Your location is read only when you clock in or out, and only to check you are on site.
clock.pinBody: Use your employee number and this PIN on a shared kiosk.
clock.pinWeak: Choose a PIN that is harder to guess.
clock.kioskLinkOnce: Open this pairing link on the kiosk now. It is shown only once.

kiosk.locked: Too many attempts. Try again later or ask your manager.
kiosk.rateLimited: Please wait a moment and try again.

onboarding.heading: Welcome to {company}, {name}
onboarding.documentsEmpty: There are no documents for you to sign.
